newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - July 28.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - July 28.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:
Westpac Banking Corp's bid for Bank of Melbourne Ltd was finally cleared by Australian authorities on Friday after four months of deliberations.

St George may have approached the Queensland government about a potential takeover of Bank of Queensland, The Sydney Morning Herald reported on Monday, citing any unnamed corporate adviser. Also in the wake of the approved Westpac/BML merger, the Australian Comptition and Consumer Commission said it would look at any proposal by National Australia Bank Ltd to take over St George Bank on its merits.

Telstra Corp and News Corp Ltd, the joint owners of pay television operator Foxtel, said on Friday that they had reached an agreement to emerge with a controlling joint stake of up to 66.5 percent in rival pay television group Australis Media Ltd. The companies said Australis would effectively acquire Foxtel from Telstra and News in exchange for new shares in Australis.

G.E. Crane reported a 41 percent rise in year net profit of A$28.945 million early on Monday. It later said it expected local business conditions to improve in the six months to December 31, 1997 and become stonger in the following six months.
CBA said it expected to open about two thirds of its branches on Monday morning as more than 25,000 of its workers attended stop-work meetings around Australia.

FAI Insurances Ltd's wholly-owned subsidiary FAI Home Loans said on Friday it has cut its standard variable home loan rate by 0.25 points to 6.64 percent in anticipation of another official cash rate cut.
